sections.title: The 'Why': Explicit vs. Implicit
sections.content: Define the difference between explicit functions (y=f(x)) and implicit equations (f(x,y)=0). Use a visual of a circle: a function passes the vertical line test, but a circle does not, requiring us to differentiate 'in-place'.
sections.example: Comparing y = sqrt(r^2 - x^2) [Explicit] vs x^2 + y^2 = r^2 [Implicit].

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Backbone
sections.content: Review the Chain Rule: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x). Emphasize that whenever we differentiate a term involving 'y' with respect to 'x', we must attach a dy/dx factor, treating y as an inner function.

sections.title: The Step-by-Step Procedure
sections.content: Introduce the 3-step algorithm: 1. Differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to x. 2. Collect all terms containing dy/dx on one side. 3. Factor out dy/dx and solve for the derivative.

sections.title: Applied Visualization: The Orbiting Satellite
sections.content: Apply the concept to a real-world scenario. Visualize a satellite moving on an elliptical path defined by an implicit equation. Calculate the slope of the velocity vector (dy/dx) at a specific coordinate point.
sections.example: Find the slope of the tangent line for the ellipse x^2 + 4y^2 = 8 at point (2, 1).

sections.title: Checklist and Recap
sections.content: Summarize key pitfalls: forgetting the Chain Rule for y-terms and sign errors during algebraic manipulation. Provide a quick visual summary chart to reinforce the mental model.
sections.example: A quick 'Golden Rule' mnemonic: 'Every time y plays, add a dy/dx to its ways!'
